original_value: Probabilistic independence is a useful concept for describing the result of random sampling—a basic operation in all probabilistic languages—and for reasoning about groups of random variables. Nevertheless, existing verification methods handle independence poorly, if at all. We propose a probabili stic separation logic PSL, where separation models probabilistic independence. We first give a new, probabilistic model of the logic of bunched implications (BI). We then build a program logic based on these assertions, and prove soundness of the proof system. We demonstrate our logic by verifying information-theoretic security of cryptographic constructions for several well-known tasks, including private information retrieval, oblivious transfer, secure multi-party addition, and simple oblivious RAM. Our proofs reason purely in terms of high-level properties, like independence and uniformity.

result.paraphrase: Probabilistic independence is a useful notion for characterizing the outcome of random sampling—a fundamental operation in all probabilistic languages—and for reasoning about collections of random variables. However, current verification techniques cope with independence poorly, if at all. We present a probabilistic separation logic, PSL, in which separation represents probabilistic independence. We first introduce a new probabilistic model of the logic of bunched implications (BI). We then construct a program logic from these assertions and prove the proof system sound. We illustrate the logic by verifying information-theoretic security for cryptographic constructions across several well-known tasks, including private information retrieval, oblivious transfer, secure multi-party addition, and simple oblivious RAM. The proofs use only high-level properties such as independence and uniformity.
